title: Define Onyx contract types (SPIDR: Interface)
spec: Write src/types.ts containing only exported TypeScript types, no runtime code. export interface CryptoEnvelope { salt: string; iv: string; tag: string; ciphertext: string } where every field is base64. export interface SecretRecord { project: string; key: string; value: string; updatedAt: number }. export interface VaultConfig { dbPath: string; passphrase: string; iterations?: number }. export type ScanRule = "private-key" | "aws-access-key" | "github-pat" | "high-entropy". export interface ScanMatch { file: string; line: number; rule: ScanRule; excerpt: string }.
acceptanceCriteria: 1. src/types.ts exports CryptoEnvelope, SecretRecord, VaultConfig, ScanRule and ScanMatch with exactly the fields named in the spec.
2. VaultConfig.iterations is optional; every other field is required.
3. The file contains no functions, classes or values: only interface and type declarations.
4. tsc -b and biome check . both pass.

title: AES-256-GCM envelopes with PBKDF2 key derivation (SPIDR: Rule)
spec: Write src/crypto.ts using only node:crypto. Import the CryptoEnvelope type with `import type { CryptoEnvelope } from "./types.js"` (relative imports must end in .js). Export: `export const DEFAULT_ITERATIONS = 100_000`; `export function deriveKey(passphrase: string, salt: Buffer, iterations: number = DEFAULT_ITERATIONS): Buffer` returning pbkdf2Sync(passphrase, salt, iterations, 32, "sha256"); `export function encrypt(plaintext: string, passphrase: string, iterations: number = DEFAULT_ITERATIONS): CryptoEnvelope` which generates a fresh randomBytes(16) salt and randomBytes(12) iv, derives the key, encrypts with createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm", key, iv), and returns salt, iv, getAuthTag() and ciphertext all as base64 strings; `export function decrypt(envelope: CryptoEnvelope, passphrase: string, iterations: number = DEFAULT_ITERATIONS): string` which reverses it. decrypt must check that the decoded iv is exactly 12 bytes and the decoded tag exactly 16 bytes, and must wrap all of its work in try/catch so that ANY failure (wrong passphrase, tampered ciphertext, tampered tag, wrong lengths) throws `new Error("decryption failed")`.
acceptanceCriteria: 1. deriveKey("password", Buffer.from("salt"), 1) returns hex 120fb6cffcf8b32c43e7225256c4f837a86548c92ccc35480805987cb70be17b.
2. DEFAULT_ITERATIONS is 100000 and deriveKey without an iterations argument uses it and returns 32 bytes.
3. decrypt(encrypt(x, p, n), p, n) returns x for ASCII, multi-byte UTF-8 and the empty string.
4. The envelope has exactly the keys salt, iv, tag, ciphertext; decoded lengths are 16, 12, 16 and the UTF-8 byte length of the plaintext.
5. Two encryptions of the same plaintext have different salt, iv and ciphertext.
6. Wrong passphrase, wrong iteration count, one flipped bit in ciphertext, tag, iv or salt, an 8-byte tag and a 16-byte iv all throw an Error whose message is exactly "decryption failed".
7. tests/crypto.spec.ts passes without modification.

title: node:sqlite WAL vault schema with constraints (SPIDR: Data)
spec: Write src/db.ts using the built-in node:sqlite module (`import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite"`; do not use better-sqlite3). Export `export function openVaultDb(path: string): DatabaseSync` which opens the file, runs PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL, PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL and PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON, then creates three tables with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS: projects (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL); secrets (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, key TEXT NOT NULL, envelope_json TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL, UNIQUE (project_id, key)); audit_events (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, action TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('set', 'get', 'list', 'delete')), project TEXT NOT NULL, key TEXT, at INTEGER NOT NULL). Also export `export function monotonicNow(previous: number, now: number = Date.now()): number` which returns now when now > previous, otherwise previous + 1.
acceptanceCriteria: 1. PRAGMA journal_mode returns wal, PRAGMA synchronous returns 1 and PRAGMA foreign_keys returns 1 on the returned connection.
2. The three tables have exactly the columns listed in the spec, no more and no fewer.
3. A duplicate project name, a duplicate (project_id, key) pair, a secret whose project_id does not exist, and an audit action outside set/get/list/delete are all rejected by SQLite.
4. Deleting a project deletes its secrets.
5. Opening the same file twice keeps existing rows.
6. monotonicNow(100, 250) is 250, monotonicNow(250, 250) is 251, monotonicNow(1000, 10) is 1001.
7. tests/db.spec.ts passes without modification.

title: Encrypted vault CRUD with transactions and audit log (SPIDR: Path)
spec: Write src/vault.ts exporting `export class Vault`. Imports (all relative imports end in .js): encrypt, decrypt, DEFAULT_ITERATIONS from "./crypto.js"; openVaultDb, monotonicNow from "./db.js"; types CryptoEnvelope, SecretRecord, VaultConfig from "./types.js". Members: `constructor(config: VaultConfig)` opens the db with openVaultDb(config.dbPath) and uses config.iterations ?? DEFAULT_ITERATIONS for every encrypt/decrypt call; `set(project: string, key: string, value: string): SecretRecord` inserts the project if missing (INSERT OR IGNORE), then upserts the secret row storing JSON.stringify(encrypt(value, ...)) in envelope_json (never the plaintext), then writes an audit_events row, all inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE / COMMIT transaction with ROLLBACK on error, and returns { project, key, value, updatedAt }; `get(project: string, key: string): string | undefined` decrypts the stored envelope or returns undefined when absent; `list(project: string): string[]` returns the project's keys sorted ascending; `delete(project: string, key: string): boolean` returns true only if a row was deleted; `env(project: string): Record<string, string>` returns every key of the project mapped to its decrypted value; `close(): void`. Every set, get, list and delete call inserts one audit_events row with action 'set', 'get', 'list' or 'delete'. Timestamps (updated_at, created_at, at) come from monotonicNow(previousTimestamp) so they strictly increase. Validation runs BEFORE any database write: a project must match /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/ else throw new Error(`invalid project: ${project}`); a key must match /^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$/ else throw new Error(`invalid key: ${key}`).
acceptanceCriteria: 1. set then get returns the value; get of a missing key or missing project returns undefined.
2. The secrets.envelope_json column never contains the plaintext and parses to an object with keys ciphertext, iv, salt, tag.
3. Setting an existing key overwrites it, list still returns it once, and the second updatedAt is strictly greater than the first.
4. list returns keys sorted ascending and only for the requested project; an unknown project gives [].
5. delete returns true once, then false; env returns { KEY: value } for one project only.
6. set("api", "lower_case", ...) throws "invalid key: lower_case"; set("Bad Project", "OK", ...) throws "invalid project: Bad Project"; after these no secrets rows and no audit rows exist.
7. Operations set, set, get, list, delete produce audit actions exactly ["set", "set", "get", "list", "delete"].
8. Data survives close and reopen; reopening with the wrong passphrase makes get throw "decryption failed".
9. tests/vault.spec.ts passes without modification.

title: Signature and Shannon-entropy secret scanner for diffs (SPIDR: Rule)
spec: Write src/scanner.ts. Import types with `import type { ScanMatch, ScanRule } from "./types.js"`. Export `export const ENTROPY_THRESHOLD = 4.0`. Export `export function shannonEntropy(text: string): number` = the sum over distinct characters of -p * Math.log2(p), where p = count / text.length; the empty string returns 0. Export `export function scanLine(line: string): { rule: ScanRule; excerpt: string } | null` which checks, in this order, and returns the FIRST hit with excerpt set to the exact matched text: rule "private-key" for /-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----/, rule "aws-access-key" for /\b(?:AKIA|ASIA)[0-9A-Z]{16}\b/, rule "github-pat" for /\bghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}\b/; if none match, it finds tokens with the global regex /[A-Za-z0-9+/_-]{20,}/g (the = sign is not a token character, so in KEY=value only value can be a token) and returns rule "high-entropy" for the first token whose shannonEntropy is >= ENTROPY_THRESHOLD; otherwise it returns null. Export `export function scanText(text: string, file: string): ScanMatch[]` which splits on "\n" and returns { file, line, rule, excerpt } for every line with a hit, where line is 1-based. Export `export function scanDiff(diff: string): ScanMatch[]` for unified git diffs: a line starting with "+++ " sets the current file to the rest of the line with a leading "b/" removed; lines starting with "--- " are skipped; a hunk header matching /^@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)(?:,\d+)? @@/ sets the current new-file line number to the captured number; a line starting with "+" is scanned (without the "+") and then advances the line number; a line starting with " " (context) advances the line number but is not scanned; lines starting with "-" and all other lines are ignored.
acceptanceCriteria: 1. shannonEntropy("abcd") is 2, shannonEntropy("aabb") is 1, shannonEntropy("0123456789abcdef") is 4, and shannonEntropy of "" or "aaaaaaaa" is 0.
2. scanLine returns { rule, excerpt } where excerpt is only the matched secret, e.g. { rule: "aws-access-key", excerpt: "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE" } for the line aws_access_key_id = AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE.
3. Signature rules win over the entropy rule on the same line.
4. A token of 20+ characters with entropy exactly 4.0 is flagged high-entropy; a 19-character random token and long low-entropy identifiers are not flagged (scanLine returns null).
5. A 19-character AKIA prefix string and a lower-case akia string are not flagged.
6. scanText reports 1-based line numbers and the given file name.

7. scanDiff reports only added lines, with new-file line numbers from the hunk header and the file name from the +++ b/ header; removed lines, context lines and the +++ header itself are never reported.
8. tests/scanner.spec.ts passes without modification.

title: Spawn child processes with secrets injected in memory (SPIDR: Path)
spec: Write src/injector.ts using spawn from node:child_process. Export `export interface RunResult { code: number | null; signal: NodeJS.Signals | null; stdout: string; stderr: string }` and `export interface RunOptions { cwd?: string; baseEnv?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv; timeoutMs?: number }`. Export `export function buildChildEnv(base: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, secrets: Record<string, string>): Record<string, string>` returning a NEW object with every base entry whose value is not undefined, then every secret (secrets override base); inputs are not mutated. Export `export function runWithSecrets(command: string, args: string[], secrets: Record<string, string>, options: RunOptions = {}): Promise<RunResult>` which calls spawn(command, args, { cwd: options.cwd ?? process.cwd(), env: buildChildEnv(options.baseEnv ?? process.env, secrets), stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"], shell: false }), collects stdout and stderr as utf8 strings, resolves on the child's "close" event with { code, signal, stdout, stderr }, rejects on the child's "error" event (for example ENOENT), and when options.timeoutMs is set kills the child with child.kill("SIGTERM") after that many milliseconds (clear the timer on close/error). Never write secrets to a file and never assign to process.env.
acceptanceCriteria: 1. buildChildEnv({ PATH: "/bin", TOKEN: "old" }, { TOKEN: "new", EXTRA: "1" }) equals { PATH: "/bin", TOKEN: "new", EXTRA: "1" }; undefined base values are dropped; neither input is mutated.
2. A child reading process.env.ONYX_API_KEY sees the injected secret; the result is exactly { code: 0, signal: null, stdout: "sk_live_999", stderr: "" }.
3. After a run, process.env of the parent does not contain the injected key and the child's working directory is still empty.
4. baseEnv replaces process.env as the base when given.
5. Exit code 3 and stderr text are propagated exactly; arguments are passed without a shell.
6. With timeoutMs 200 a never-ending child resolves with code null and signal "SIGTERM".
7. A command that does not exist rejects with an error mentioning ENOENT.
8. tests/injector.spec.ts passes without modification.

title: CLI argument parser and ANSI color formatting (SPIDR: Interface)
spec: Write src/cli.ts with no imports. Export `export type Command = { kind: "set"; project: string; key: string; value: string } | { kind: "get"; project: string; key: string } | { kind: "list"; project: string } | { kind: "run"; project: string; command: string; args: string[] } | { kind: "scan" } | { kind: "export"; project: string; out: string } | { kind: "error"; message: string }`. Export `export type Color = "red" | "green" | "yellow"` and `export function colorize(text: string, color: Color, enabled: boolean): string` returning `\x1b[31m` + text + `\x1b[0m` for red (32 for green, 33 for yellow) when enabled, and text unchanged when not enabled. Export `export function parseArgs(argv: string[]): Command`. Parsing: split argv at the first "--"; everything after it is the run command and its args, kept verbatim. Before "--", a "--project NAME" pair may appear anywhere and sets project (default "default"); if "--project" has no following value return error "missing value for --project". The remaining words are the command name and its positional arguments. Grammar and error messages (return { kind: "error", message }): no command -> "usage: onyx COMMAND"; set needs exactly KEY VALUE -> "usage: onyx set KEY VALUE"; get needs exactly KEY -> "usage: onyx get KEY"; list takes no arguments -> "usage: onyx list"; run takes no positional arguments and requires "--" followed by at least a command -> "usage: onyx run -- CMD ARGS..."; scan takes no arguments -> "usage: onyx scan"; export needs exactly FILE -> "usage: onyx export FILE"; any other name -> `unknown command: ${name}`.
acceptanceCriteria: 1. parseArgs(["set", "API_KEY", "abc"]) equals { kind: "set", project: "default", key: "API_KEY", value: "abc" }.
2. --project works before or after the command name.
3. parseArgs(["run", "--project", "api", "--", "pnpm", "dev", "--project", "x"]) equals { kind: "run", project: "api", command: "pnpm", args: ["dev", "--project", "x"] }.
4. parseArgs(["scan"]) equals { kind: "scan" } with no other properties.
5. Every usage error in the spec returns exactly the listed message, including too many arguments.
6. colorize("ok", "green", true) is "\x1b[32mok\x1b[0m" and colorize("plain", "red", false) is "plain".
7. tests/cli.spec.ts passes without modification.

title: Wire the CLI to vault, injector, scanner and export (SPIDR: Integration)
spec: Write src/app.ts. Imports (relative imports end in .js): parseArgs from "./cli.js", encrypt from "./crypto.js", runWithSecrets from "./injector.js", scanDiff from "./scanner.js", Vault from "./vault.js", plus execFileSync from node:child_process, writeFileSync from node:fs and resolve from node:path. Export `export interface CliIO { dbPath: string; passphrase: string; cwd: string; iterations?: number; out: (line: string) => void; err: (line: string) => void }` and `export async function runCli(argv: string[], io: CliIO): Promise<number>` returning the exit code. Behaviour by parsed command: error -> io.err(message), return 2, and do NOT open the vault. scan -> run execFileSync("git", ["diff", "--cached", "--no-color"], { cwd: io.cwd, encoding: "utf8" }), call scanDiff, io.out(`${file}:${line} ${rule}`) per match, return 1 if any match else 0 (no vault). All other commands open new Vault({ dbPath, passphrase, iterations }) (only pass iterations when io.iterations is defined) and always close it in a finally block: set -> vault.set, io.out(`set ${key}`), return 0; get -> io.out(value) and return 0, or io.err(`not found: ${key}`) and return 1; list -> io.out(key) per key, return 0; run -> runWithSecrets(command, args, vault.env(project), { cwd: io.cwd }), io.out(stdout) if stdout is non-empty, io.err(stderr) if non-empty, return code ?? 1; export -> encrypt(JSON.stringify(vault.env(project)), io.passphrase, io.iterations), write JSON.stringify(envelope) to resolve(io.cwd, out), io.out(`exported ${count} secrets to ${out}`), return 0. Any thrown Error in these commands -> io.err(error.message), return 1.
acceptanceCriteria: 1. set, set, list, get produce out lines exactly ["set API_KEY", "set DB_URL", "API_KEY", "DB_URL", "sk_live_1"] with exit codes 0.
2. get of a missing key returns 1 with err ["not found: NOPE"].
3. An unknown command returns 2, reports "unknown command: frobnicate", and does not create the database file.
4. set with an invalid key returns 1 with err ["invalid key: bad-key"].
5. run injects the project's secrets into the child (out contains "token=tok_123"), only that project's secrets, returns the child's exit code, and leaves the working directory empty.
6. export writes an encrypted file that does not contain the plaintext and decrypts with the passphrase to { A: "alpha", B: "beta" }.
7. scan returns 1 and outputs "config.env:2 aws-access-key" when a staged file contains an AWS key, and returns 0 with no output when only unstaged files contain secrets.
8. tests/e2e.spec.ts passes without modification.
